observation.visible_scene: A close, fixed shot of a beige spiky-textured sphere resting in a white three-petal star-shaped cradle (a soft-robotic gripper), with metal servo/motor housings visible at left and right and a bundle of multicolored wires at lower left against a uniform blue background. The cradle, motors, wires and framing stay in the same place throughout; the only moving element is the spiky ball held inside the cradle.
visible_changes: The spiky ball continuously rotates in place within the stationary cradle: the diamond-spike surface pattern shifts and tilts across the visible face from frame to frame.
Small dark surface markers (three dots clustered near the top early on) drift toward the right side of the ball and out of view as the rotation proceeds.

A seam/parting line on the ball becomes visible and its apparent orientation changes over time (roughly vertical, then diagonal, then vertical again), consistent with the ball spinning about an axis near the viewing direction; a single dark dot sits on this seam and moves with it.
The relative position of the ball's features to the fixed white petals changes, while the petals themselves do not move.
The blue background and the metal actuator positions remain constant, indicating no camera pan/zoom and no gripper motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What drives the ball's rotation (a hidden actuator, the gripper twisting it, or external contact) is not visible in this segment.
Whether the rotation begins before or continues after this excerpt, and the ball's material identity, are not shown.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation axis and sense (clockwise vs counter-clockwise) cannot be pinned down from the surface features alone.

It is unclear whether the ball is a single rigid body spinning or two hemispherical shells rotating relative to each other, since the spike pattern on either side of the seam appears to differ in later frames.
Whether the seam is a molded parting line, a crack, or a deliberate feature is not determinable from the images.
